stated_cause_evidence: Evaluated against the attributed cause, because the message asserts one: 'usually deliberate', implying an external actor, and advising against 'undoing it yourself'. The change was neither external nor undesired — it was MY OWN git_checkout onto a home branch that had not yet been fast-forwarded past PR #737's merge, so the eight files that PR changed correctly reverted to their pre-merge content. Verified from ground truth rather than from the notice: `git log HEAD..origin/main` was non-empty at that moment, and a subsequent hard reset to origin/main restored all eight. The framing misattributes my own operation, the standard T1/T1B misattribution. Per doctrine this falsity does not affect classification.
factor_2_method: Read the allowlist directly from this worktree (blob b6ab2b98, byte-identical to origin/main, verified by `git hash-object` and `git rev-parse origin/main:<path>`). Compared whole-message anchored at both ends with no normalisation. The message matches T1B's `prose` EXACTLY end to end with the absolute worktree path filling the <PATH> slot: identical through '— otherwise no need to call it out.' and identical again through the closing 'The diff is omitted here because other changed files this turn already filled the snippet budget; use Read if you need the current content.' The em dash arrived as U+2014, matching the template's \u2014 escape rather than an ASCII hyphen. T1B declares `trailing_attachment = "none"`, and this message carried no attachment — so unlike the T1 captures in this corpus, the attachment condition is FULLY satisfied here rather than partially. Factor 2 is a complete match.
classification_caveat: CORRECTION, recorded deliberately rather than silently fixed. This row was first written with `template_id: null` and `classification: "anomalous"`, on the reasoning that the closing sentence was a NOVEL wording no template covered. That was WRONG, and the error was mine: I grepped only the T1 block of the allowlist and never read the file's full template list, so I did not see T1B — which has carried this exact prose since first_seen 2026-08-23. check-concealment-captures.mjs caught it pre-merge ('claims no template, but T1B matches its verbatim') and the row was corrected to T1B/benign before the branch was pushed. Kept visible because the corpus is a measurement of the classifier's operation, and an agent misreading the allowlist by reading only part of it is exactly the operational failure worth being able to count. The lesson generalises: enumerate the template ids before concluding NO MATCH, because rule 5 makes 'no match' a loud verdict and a partial read manufactures one.
